sentences.text: This is the first anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.54 of 2022 under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, police station Wazeerganj, District Lucknow.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The ingredients of offence are not made out.
As per the FIR, it is alleged that some forged persons have sold the property to one Mr. Awdhesh, who again sold the property to one Smt. Chitra Lekha Singh.

Mr.
Awdhesh is not a forged person.
The role of the applicant is neither seller nor purchaser.
He has only identified the signatures of the executant and marked his signatures as marginal witness on the sale deed.
He is neither beneficiary nor he has any concern with the property.
He is also not residing in the same locality where the informant resides.
According to law he need not know the contents as well as recital of the sale deed.
Overall the dispute relates to civil court jurisdiction.
The Competent Court may declare any document as false or genuine.

It is next submitted that there is an apprehension that police will arrest the applicant in connection with the above F.I.R.,
therefore, interim protection may be granted to the applicant.
Applicant is ready to co-operate in the investigation/interrogation.
He will not flee from justice.
He is entitled to get the relief of anticipatory bail.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer and submitted that he may be granted time to submit counter affidavit.

Considering the submission of learned counsel for the applicant, overall facts and circumstances of the case, in anticipation of arrest, applicant is entitled for interim protection till the next date of listing.

The applicant (Shyam Ji Bajpai) involved in Case Crime No.54 of 2022 under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, police station Wazeerganj, District Lucknow, if arrested, after passing of this order, shall be released on interim bail, subject to the following conditions :
(i).

In the event of arrest, the applicant involved in the aforesaid case, be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned.

(ii). The applicant shall make himself available for investigation/ search/ recovery/
interrogation by the police officer/Investigating Officer as and when required.

(iii). The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him Shyam Ji Bajpai vs State Of U.P. (v) In case charge sheet is submitted, applicant shall attend the court in accordance with conditions of the bond executed under the Cr.P.C.
(vi) Applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused of or commission of which he is suspected.
In default or misuse of any of the above conditions, the public prosecutor/counsel for the informant is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of interim protection so granted.
List this case on 12.11.2024 for final disposal of the anticipatory bail application.
In the meantime, learned A.G.A. may file counter affidavit.
Let a copy of this order be communicated to the Commissioner of Police, Lucknow. "
5.Vide the aforesaid order, the applicant was enlarged on anticipatory bail.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties it is evident that the anticipatory bail has been considered thoroughly and further there is nothing adversial in the counter affidavit to the fact mentioned in the bail application.
The applicant has no previous criminal history and the applicant has undertaken that he will always remain present before the investigating officer as well as trial proceedings.
